Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A strong thermal day with a sharp 10.0 °C/km lapse rate, maximum domain-wide thermal strength of 666 ft/min, and clear skies. Increasing afternoon winds at several sites and widespread low-level shear will require careful site selection; many launches are only suitable for advanced pilots due to rough, powerful thermals.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — brief soarable window 9am–10am with SE winds aligning before shifting cross; peak w* 371 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3311 ft AGL.
  • Hallelujah: Favorable (advanced pilots only — sharp lapse rate 9.9 °C/km) — strong thermals and ridge-lift W winds 11am–5pm; peak w* 531 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5433 ft AGL.
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — persistent strong SW winds off launch direction and low-level shear 7 mph at 241 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Marginal — good thermals and S‑SW winds 10am–12pm, then veering W off direction; peak w* 403 ft/min, ceiling ~2000 ft AGL.
  • West McClellan: Marginal — strong W winds become aligned after noon with usable thermals; peak w* 378 ft/min, ceiling 2669 ft AGL; suited to experienced ridge soaring.
  • Peavine Mountain: Unfavorable — strong SW winds outside the preferred range and sharp lapse rate 9.9 °C/km, making conditions hazardous.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal (advanced) — brief NE ridge window at 10am with light wind, then wind veers off; sharp lapse rate 10.1 °C/km; peak w* 328 ft/min, ceiling 2064 ft AGL.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable (advanced pilots only — sharp lapse rate 10.1 °C/km) — strong thermals and soarable NW‑N winds from midday; peak w* 581 ft/min, thermal ceiling >8000 ft AGL; window 12pm–6pm.
  • Daydreams: Favorable — rideable SW winds 10am–5pm with light thermals; peak w* 234 ft/min, ceiling up to 4261 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate 8.9 °C/km demands advanced caution.

Hazards

  • Sharp lapse rate (>8 °C/km) at Hallelujah, Peavine, Rainbow Ridge, Duck Hill, and Daydreams — powerful, rough thermals suitable only for advanced/expert pilots.
  • Low-level speed shear ≥5 mph per layer at Kingsbury (6 mph at 247 ft), Slide Mountain (7 mph at 241 ft), West McClellan (5 mph at 1,529 ft), Peavine (6 mph at 240 ft), Rainbow Ridge (7 mph at 8,184 ft), Duck Hill (10 mph at 7,750 ft), and Daydreams (6 mph at 4,386 ft) — increased turbulence and risk of collapses.
  • Rotor and lee turbulence likely downwind of Peavine Mtn and Carson Range ridgelines, especially with the strong SW flow.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
